title: 结点电压法：电压源接在参考结点上
statement: 图示电路中 V_s = 20 V，I_s = 2 A（向上注入结点 c），R_1 = 2 Ω，R_2 = 6 Ω，R_3 = 2 Ω，R_4 = 2 Ω。以底部为参考结点。
用**结点电压法**求 v_b、v_c，以及电压源 V_s 吸收的功率。

questions.ask: 本电路有 3 个独立结点 a、b、c，为什么只需要列 2 个结点方程？
choices: 结点 a 的电压已知 v_a = V_s，不必对 a 列方程
电压源支路的电导为零，可以去掉
结点 a 与 c 的方程总是相同的
电压源可以等效为开路
choiceExplain: 理想电压源的电流由外电路决定，不能写成“电导 × 电压”，它的电导不是零；去掉它电路就变了（v_a 不再是 20 V）。
a、c 两结点连接的元件不同，KCL 方程一般不同，并不是因为方程相同才少列一个。
电压源只有在置零（叠加定理中）时才变成短路，从来不是开路；在这里它把 v_a 定为 20 V。
questions.explain: 电压源一端接参考结点，另一端结点的电压直接等于 V_s = 20 V，这个结点不再是未知量；而且电压源电流无法用结点电压表示，本来也不能对 a 用电导形式列 KCL。
V_s 输出的电流就是 R_1 的电流 (20 − 12)/2 = 4 A，从“+”端流出：P = −20 × 4 = −80 W（发出 80 W）。

hints: 用结点电压法。先看哪个结点电压已经由电压源直接确定——它不是未知量，剩下的结点电压才需要列方程。
电流源 I_s 注入结点 c：它的电流直接写在结点 c 方程的右边，不需要知道它两端的电压。
代表方程（结点 b）：(1/R_1 + 1/R_2 + 1/R_3)v_b − (1/R_1)v_a − (1/R_3)v_c = 0，已知的 v_a 项移到右边；结点 c 照此写出，两式联立。
solution: **1. 已知结点：** V_s 接在 a 与参考结点之间，v_a = **20 V**。

en.title: Nodal analysis: a voltage source tied to the reference node
statement: In the circuit, V_s = 20 V, I_s = 2 A (upwards, into node c), R_1 = 2 Ω, R_2 = 6 Ω, R_3 = 2 Ω, R_4 = 2 Ω. The bottom node is the reference.
Use **nodal analysis** to find v_b, v_c and the power absorbed by the voltage source V_s.

questions.ask: The circuit has 3 independent nodes a, b and c. Why are only 2 node equations needed?
choices: The voltage of node a is known, v_a = V_s, so no equation is written for a
The voltage-source branch has zero conductance and can be removed
The equations of nodes a and c are always identical
A voltage source can be replaced by an open circuit
choiceExplain: The current of an ideal voltage source is set by the rest of the circuit and can't be written as conductance × voltage — its conductance is not zero; removing it changes the circuit (v_a would no longer be 20 V).
Nodes a and c connect to different elements, so their KCL equations are generally different; the saved equation is not due to their being identical.
A voltage source becomes a short only when it is zeroed (in superposition), never an open; here it fixes v_a at 20 V.
questions.explain: One end of the voltage source is the reference node, so the other node's voltage is simply V_s = 20 V and is no longer an unknown. Besides, the source current can't be expressed through node voltages, so a conductance-form KCL at a isn't possible anyway.
With v_a = 20 V the two equations are (1/2 + 1/6 + 1/2)v_b − 0.5v_c = 10 and −0.5v_b + v_c = 2, giving v_b = 12 V.
The source current equals the current in R_1, (20 − 12)/2 = 4 A, leaving the "+" terminal: P = −20 × 4 = −80 W (it delivers 80 W).

hints: Use nodal analysis. First see which node voltage is fixed directly by the voltage source — it is not an unknown; only the remaining node voltages need equations.
The current source I_s injects into node c: its current goes straight onto the right-hand side of node c's equation; you don't need the voltage across it.
A representative equation (node b): (1/R_1 + 1/R_2 + 1/R_3)v_b − (1/R_1)v_a − (1/R_3)v_c = 0, with the known v_a term moved to the right; write node c the same way and solve the pair.
solution: **1. Known node:** V_s sits between a and the reference, so v_a = **20 V**.
**5. Source power:** i_R1 = (20 − 12)/2 = 4 A leaves the "+" terminal of V_s, so P_Us = −20 × 4 = **−80 W** (delivers 80 W).
**Check:** the resistors absorb 2×4² + 12²/6 + 2×2² + 8²/2 = 32 + 24 + 8 + 32 = 96 W; V_s delivers 80 W and I_s delivers 8 × 2 = 16 W, 96 W in total.
